list.name: Changes
list.comment:
Debug cleanup — Removed the debug parameter and all print statements from get_scores and the CLI. The include_fails="1" param stayed since it's correct behaviour.
--- normalize.py — Three functions: - clean_title — runs each noise pattern (TV Size, Short Ver., feat., etc.) against the title and strips matches - normalize_for_comparison — applies clean_title, then converts unicode to ASCII via NFKD decomposition (e.g. café → cafe), lowercases, and collapses whitespace. This is what gets passed into the fuzzy scorer, not the Spotify search string - best_title / best_artist — pick the romanized version if available, otherwise try to convert unicode to ASCII. This is what gets used as the Spotify search query, so the search stays readable while the comparison stays strict
--- spotify_api.py — Four functions: - get_client — sets up Spotipy with SpotifyOAuth using your credentials and the two playlist scopes. First run will open a browser for login - search_track — tries a strict query (track:"..." artist:"...") first, falls back to a plain artist title query if nothing comes back - create_playlist — creates a new playlist under the authenticated user's account - add_tracks — adds URIs to a playlist in chunks of 100 (Spotify's hard limit per request)
--- matching.py — Three functions: - _score — computes 0.65 * title_similarity + 0.35 * artist_similarity using rapidfuzz.fuzz.token_sort_ratio, which handles word-order differences gracefully - match_song — for one song: picks the best search strings via normalize, calls search_track, scores all candidates, picks the highest, and classifies it as matched (≥85), review (≥70), or unmatched (<70) - match_songs — maps match_song over the full list
--- cli.py — match-spotify command — Reads a CSV back into OsuSong objects, authenticates with Spotify, runs matching, prints a matched/review/unmatched summary, and writes both output CSVs. The command is now fully wired.
Usage: python -m OsuSongParser match-spotify --input exports/most_played.csv

task.summary: Initialize Project: Create files and necessary directories

models.py — Wrote the two dataclasses from the PDF verbatim, with one addition: tags: str | None on OsuSong (Issue 5 fix). Everything else is as specified.
config.py — Loads .env via python-dotenv and exposes all the env vars from Section 9 as typed module-level constants. Nothing fancy — just a single place to import config from instead of sprinkling os.getenv calls across the codebase.
local_osu.py — Three functions: - _parse_osu_file — reads a .osu file, walks line by line, only collects keys from [General] and [Metadata] sections - _build_song — turns the raw key/value dict into an OsuSong. Prefers Unicode fields over ASCII, handles -1 beatmap IDs (osu! uses -1 for "no ID"), builds the osu! URLs - scan_local — recursively globs for *.osu, deduplicates by BeatmapSetID first, falls back to casefold artist|title key, returns one entry per beatmapset
export.py — Four functions for writing the four output files the spec defines: export_songs_csv, export_songs_json, export_matches_csv, export_unmatched_csv. Uses dataclasses.asdict to serialize OsuSong cleanly.
cli.py — Four commands registered with Typer matching the spec exactly (scan-local, fetch-osu, match-spotify, create-playlist). Only scan-local is wired up. The other three print "not implemented yet" and exit with code 1 — they're stubs so the CLI is already discoverable via --help.
normalize.py — Just the agreed-upon pattern list for now (no logic yet). The broad r"\[.*?\]" is absent. This file gets its actual implementation in MVP 3 when Spotify matching is built.

osu_api.py
- OsuApiClient — holds the session and token. _ensure_token() fetches a client credentials token on the first call and caches it in memory with a 60-second expiry buffer. _get() attaches the bearer token automatically. - get_scores() — single request, respects the API cap (50 for recent, 100 for best/firsts), passes include_fails=1 for recent automatically. - get_beatmapsets() — offset-loop pagination, fetches 100 at a time until limit is reached or the API returns fewer than requested. - Three converter functions handle the two distinct response shapes: songs_from_scores, songs_from_most_played (beatmap → beatmapset nesting), and songs_from_beatmapsets (top-level beatmapset). All three deduplicate by beatmapset_id.
cli.py — fetch-osu command
- Validates --type upfront and rejects unknown values with a clear error listing valid options. - Checks that credentials are present before making any network call. - Score types show the API cap so the user understands why raising --limit won't help there. - Beatmapset types show the limit used, and if results hit the ceiling, prints the yellow hint with a doubled --limit suggestion.
